name: What types of wood are most resistant to rot?

mainEntity.name: What types of wood are most resistant to rot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Certain types of wood offer higher natural resistance to rot due to their density and natural compounds. These include cedar, redwood, cypress, and pressure-treated lumber. Pressure-treated wood, often used for outdoor applications or ground contact, is infused with chemicals that deter fungal growth and insects. When planning a repair, considering these materials, especially in moisture-prone areas, can significantly extend the lifespan of the repaired section and reduce future maintenance. We often recommend pressure-treated lumber for external repairs in our service areas of Meridian, Eagle, and Kuna.
acceptedAnswer.description: Cedar, redwood, cypress, and pressure-treated lumber are most rot-resistant. Using these materials, especially pressure-treated lumber for external repairs, extends longevity.
